_meta: Externally-researched circuit-optimization techniques injected into Aristotle prompts by gen_prompts.py. Techniques are candidate ideas from the ZK literature — the Clean challenge is R1CS with cost = allocations + constraints, so some lookup/GKR/sumcheck tricks may NOT map; Aristotle must verify applicability before use. Refreshed periodically via web research.
_common: MECHANICAL POST-PASS over the finished constraint system (arkworks r1cs-optimizer passes): (a) DEAD VARIABLE ELIMINATION — drop every allocated witness never read by a surviving constraint; (b) CONSTRAINT DEDUPLICATION — identical rank-1 rows collapse to one; (c) CONSTANT FOLDING; (d) LINEAR SUBSTITUTION — a variable defined by an affine constraint is inlined into its uses and both it and its defining row disappear. Cost here is allocations+constraints, so each pass pays twice; run this sweep at the END of any rewrite, since hand-golfing reliably leaves orphaned witnesses behind.

GAUSSIAN-ELIMINATION DISTILLING (Albert et al., CAV 2022, 'Distilling Constraints in Zero-Knowledge Protocols', implemented in circom): run Gaussian elimination over the NON-LINEAR constraint set to DEDUCE previously implicit LINEAR constraints, then use those to substitute away variables and delete rows — strictly stronger than plain linear substitution, because it finds linear facts implied only by the quadratic rows. Reported up to 16.33% of constraints removed from circomlib circuits that had ALREADY been hand-simplified — assume a hand-golfed circuit still hides redundancy, and re-run this after every rewrite. HOW TO ACTUALLY RUN IT (circom --O2 mechanics, docs.circom.io/circom-language/circom-insight/simplification): collect the MAXIMAL CLUSTERS of linear constraints that share signals and solve each cluster in one go with a lazy Gauss-Jordan pass, rather than substituting one row at a time; then iterate to FIXPOINT — after substitution some constraints that were non-linear BECOME linear, so repeat rounds until no eliminable linear constraint remains. SCOPING RULE: only a constraint containing at least one PRIVATE signal may be eliminated; interface inputs/outputs are fixed by the challenge and can never be substituted away. IN CLEAN THIS IS CONCRETE: any value you `witness` that is an AFFINE function of values already in scope is pure waste — affine combinations are free Expressions here, so inline it and delete its assertEq. That removes 1 allocation AND 1 constraint, i.e. 2 units of score per elimination. Do this sweep LAST, after the circuit shape is final, and re-prove the affected theorems.

CLEAN STRUCTURING IDIOM (zksecurity, 'Verifying Poseidon in Clean'): wrap each repeated block in its OWN FormalCircuit and drive it with Circuit.foldl instead of unfolding every iteration inline — unfolding makes the elaborated term enormous and elaboration 'slow and brittle', which is the usual reason an aggressive rewrite cannot close its proofs and ends up returning `sorry`. Applies directly to all five challenges: 64 SHA-256 rounds, 24 Keccak rounds, the 17 RSA squarings/multiplies, the per-bit scalar-mul ladder. Conversely keep CHEAP AFFINE work (round constants, linear/matrix layers) INLINE — factoring it into its own circuit obscures the proof without lowering cost. localLength must account for EVERY intermediate witness, so count per-iteration allocations exactly (Poseidon reference: 6 per partial round vs 8 per full round) — that count IS half the score.
sha256-hash: Majority(B,C,D) = (B&C) ^ (B&D) ^ (C&D): three ANDs + XOR-fold; Ch(E,F,G) = G ^ (E&(F^G)) uses ONE AND (E&(F^G)) instead of two.

Represent each 32-bit word's bits once and reuse; XOR / rotation / shift are FREE affine combinations of bit variables — never allocate constraints for them, only for the AND (booleanity + one rank-1 product).

CALIBRATION: an optimized pure-R1CS circom SHA-256 compression costs 26,170 nonlinear constraints (bkomuves/hash-circuits), ~13% below circomlib — treat ~26k constraints/compression as the bar a straightforward good encoding already clears.
Carry-save (3:2 compressor) addition to combine the 6-7 addends in the round function before a single final modular reduction, rather than chained 2-input adds.
Fold the top bit of every 32-bit range decomposition (prove the MSB via the boolean already forced elsewhere) to save one boolean per word.

Smart bitwidth adjustment (xJsnark): track a STATIC upper bound on every intermediate 32-bit word through the adds/XOR-folds and insert a bit-decomposition/normalization ONLY when that bound would overflow the native field — not after every operation. Reported ~3.2k constraints saved vs Geppetto and ~10k vs Buffet on SHA-256; each skipped decomposition removes 32 allocations + its booleanity constraints, so it pays double in this metric.

Global common-subexpression / multivariate-polynomial minimization across the 64 rounds (xJsnark, reported ~8.8k constraints on SHA-256): the message schedule and round function reuse the same sigma/XOR-fold subexpressions — allocate each distinct affine combination ONCE and share it everywhere rather than per-round.

If the framework exposes lookups: 'spread'/interleaved-bit tables (Barretenberg-style) turn XOR3 and Maj into table reads; only worth it if a lookup is cheaper than the ~1 constraint the arithmetic form already costs — verify against this R1CS cost model first.

Boyar-Peralta counter bound also applies to the NATIVE SHA-256 challenge's bit-level adders: MC of Hamming weight of n bits is exactly n - H(n), so multi-operand column addition wants optimal k:log(k) counters, not chained 3:2 compressors. Weigh against the field-arithmetic route here (a native field can add many 32-bit words in one linear combination and range-check once) — pick whichever costs fewer allocations+constraints, but do not assume chained full adders are optimal.
keccak-f1600: THE OPTIMIZATION IS ALREADY SOLVED HERE — ONLY THE PROOF IS MISSING. This is the ONLY challenge whose seed is the BASELINE (153600 alloc + 153600 constraints = 307200, i.e. 4.0+4.0 per bit) rather than a verified record, because the 184320 record omits computableWitness. But that record's FULL SOURCE is in reference/ and declares exactly 92160 allocations + 92160 constraints (3840/round, 2.4+2.4 per bit). So do NOT spend effort re-deriving the 40% reduction — PORT the reference circuit shape verbatim and spend essentially all effort CONSTRUCTING A FULLY-PROVED computableWitness for it (adapt the baseline's, which does have one). That single proof obligation is the whole task, and is presumably why the record holder stopped short.
theta/rho/pi are pure linear XOR + fixed rotations — keep them as FREE affine combinations; charge constraints ONLY for bit booleanity and chi.
chi_i = a_i ^ ((¬a_{i+1}) & a_{i+2}); ¬b = 1-b is affine, so chi is ONE rank-1 AND plus an XOR-fold per bit — 3200 constraints/round is the target to beat.

Optional ±1 (Fourier) basis where true=-1,false=+1: XOR becomes a single multiplication and negation is free (Keccacheck); can collapse some XOR-chains — verify it doesn't inflate the booleanity/const-folding cost in R1CS.

CALIBRATION: an optimized pure-R1CS circom implementation (bkomuves/hash-circuits) reaches 144,830 nonlinear constraints for ONE Keccak-f1600 compression, vs 185,856 for the naive encoding that charges 4480/round for theta. If your constraint count sits near 185k, theta is still being paid for — it must be free affine combinations.

SHARPENING OF THE ABOVE (arithmetic, verify it): 184320 / 24 = 7680 = 4480 + 3200 EXACTLY — the leaderboard record is paying the NAIVE 4480/round theta plus 3200/round chi, with iota's constant XOR already free. Since bkomuves' pure-R1CS Keccak reaches 144830 by making theta affine, roughly 40k of headroom sits in THETA alone, and chi at 3200 (one mul per state bit) is already at/near the multiplicative-complexity floor. Spend the effort on theta's 320 five-bit column parities C[x] and the 1600 A ^= D XORs — sum-then-extract-parity (allocate parity p and a 2-bit quotient q, enforce b0+..+b4 = p+2q) rather than chaining 4 pairwise a+b-2ab products — NOT on shaving chi.
iota XORs a round constant — a pure affine offset, zero constraints.

NOTE: the leaderboard record (184320) omits computableWitness; reproduce its circuit shape on the valid baseline AND add a fully-proved computableWitness. GKR/sum-check results (<4k) are a DIFFERENT proof system and do not transfer to this R1CS metric.

COST DIAGNOSIS (derived — verify before trusting): the record 184320 = 1600 bits x 24 rounds x 4.8. The sibling GF(2) challenge does the SAME permutation shape at 2.0 per bit-round (1 allocation + 1 constraint = just chi's product). The whole 2.8/bit gap is XOR OVERHEAD: over the circom prime a XOR b = a + b - 2ab costs a MULTIPLICATION, whereas over GF(2) it is free addition. So the entire remaining win on this challenge is in how XOR is encoded — not in chi, whose multiplicative complexity is already minimal (5 per 5-bit row, SAT-proven).

SUM-THEN-EXTRACT-PARITY for wide XORs (the main lever): to XOR k bits over a large prime field, do NOT chain k-1 pairwise a+b-2ab products. Instead form S = b_1 + ... + b_k as a FREE affine combination (zero constraints), then extract S mod 2 by decomposing S into ceil(log2(k+1)) bits with one linear equation S = 2q + r; the parity bit r IS the XOR. Cost ~log2(k) allocations + booleanity instead of (k-1) multiplications. theta XORs 5 lane bits plus a rotated column parity (k~5-11), where log2 beats linear decisively — this is how theta becomes near-free in a NON-binary field.

FOLD BOOLEANITY INTO THE PRODUCT: if c = a*b with a,b already known boolean, c is automatically boolean — do NOT emit a separate c(c-1)=0 row. Likewise the parity bit from a sum-decomposition is forced boolean by the range argument. Every redundant booleanity row is a pure loss at 1 constraint each, and at 38400 chi outputs that is 38400 constraints if repeated.
rsa-pkcs1v15-sha256-4096-65537: CORRECTION — THERE IS NO SHA-256 IN THIS CIRCUIT. Verified against the challenge interface: `digest : Vector F digestBytesLen` is an INPUT ('SHA-256 digest of the message being verified'), and the seed solution contains zero hash/compression files — every module is bigint machinery (SqMulModBal, ModExpSq, GroupedEq*, EqViaCarries, MixedRadix, Bytes*). The published '66% SHA-2 / 14% bigint' split for RS256 circuits does NOT apply here because those circuits hash the message and this one does not. ALL ~326k of the cost is non-native bigint arithmetic: the 16 squarings + 1 multiply mod a 4096-bit N, plus byte<->limb conversion and the padding comparison. Optimise the modmul and the limb/carry machinery; do not go looking for a hash to shrink.
Exponent 65537 = 2^16 + 1: exactly 16 squarings + 1 multiply; every step is a fixed-modulus modmul — share reduction machinery across all 17.
Fixed modulus: precompute q'[0] (Montgomery -N^{-1} mod 2^w), R^2 mod N, and all modulus limbs as circuit CONSTANTS — no in-circuit inverse or per-op setup.
CIOS/Montgomery with carry elimination: when the top modulus word is bounded ((D-1)/2-1), the t[N]/t[N+1] carries are provably zero, dropping ~5N+2 additions per multiply (gnark result).
Limb count sweet spot N<=12 wide limbs; minimize the number of carries that need range checks — each naive range check costs ~1/2 constraint per bit, so wider limbs with fewer carries win.
CRT / RNS residue representation to split the 4096-bit reduce into independent smaller-modulus channels; recombine once at the end.
Only range-check the modular residual, the quotient coefficient, and carries — not every intermediate; use top-bit-fold range checks.

LAZY REDUCTION with static limb-bound tracking (xJsnark long-integer arithmetic): carry a compile-time upper bound per limb and let partial products accumulate in wider limbs; emit a carry-normalization + range check ONLY when a limb's tracked bound would exceed field capacity, instead of normalizing after every op. Across the 16 squarings + 1 multiply this removes whole normalization passes, not just individual carries.

DEFERRAL BUDGET, concretely (circom-ecdsa): with n-bit limbs and k of them, unreduced accumulation is safe while 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < (native field bits). Use this inequality to place carry/reduce passes at the LAST legal moment instead of guessing; multiples of the fixed modulus used to reduce are compile-time constants.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce): keep products unreduced in wide limbs and reduce once per accumulated expression, not per multiply. CAUTION: bellman-bignat [OWWB20] and similar bigint libraries are tuned for constraint DENSITY, not constraint COUNT — do not copy their limb layout without re-costing it against allocations+constraints.

mulmod as ONE polynomial-identity check at a single constant point (gnark/eprint 2025/933): hint quotient q and error/carry limbs e out of circuit, then enforce a(X)b(X) = c(X) + alpha(X)q(X) + (2^B - X)e(X) evaluated at ONE fixed X=2^B — collapses the full limb-by-limb equality into a single rank-1 product plus range checks on q,c,e, instead of one constraint per limb coefficient. Evaluate-at-a-point beats coefficient-matching in this R1CS metric; reuse the same hinted-then-checked shape for all 17 squarings/multiplies.

PKCS1v15 padding is almost entirely CONSTANT: the 0x00 01 FF...FF 00 prefix and the DigestInfo DER header are fixed bytes. Comparing the recovered padded block against them costs only affine equality checks against constants — allocate nothing for the padding bytes themselves, and never range-check a byte whose value is fixed by the spec.
secp256k1-scalar-mul: BIGGEST STRUCTURAL GAP vs THE FIXED-BASE SIBLING: NEVER WITNESS y IN THE LOOP (halo2 variable-base scalar-mul gadget). Measured on the 563079 seed: glvMSM 247095+248985 = 496080 (88% of the circuit), built from ~65 FusedStep at 3785/3815 = 7600 each, and each FusedStep ends in finishXY 1482/1494 = 2976 that MATERIALIZES BOTH x AND y. halo2 never assigns y inside the loop: it keeps (x_A, lambda) and derives y algebraically — lambda1*(x_A - x_T) = y_A - (2k-1)*y_T, lambda2^2 = x_A_prev + x_R + x_A, x_R = lambda1^2 - x_A - x_T, and y_A = (lambda1 + lambda2)*(x_A - x_R)/2 — so y is 'implicitly derived from lambda1, lambda2, x_A, x_T but never actually assigned', and is witnessed ONLY at the final iteration. The sibling fixed-base solution already does exactly this (ChainExt 1462/1471 = 2933 per step carrying (x,lam), with a single ChainFinish materializing y), which is why its per-step add is 2.6x cheaper than this one's. Port the (x, lambda) recurrence into the GLV MSM loop and materialize y ONCE at the end: the y-materialization alone is ~2976 x 65 = ~193k rows (~34% of the circuit), and even partial recovery of it dwarfs any table or recoding tweak. Verify the exact split in your copy before rewriting.

MONTGOMERY-LADDER / x-ONLY IS THE WRONG DIRECTION HERE — DO NOT SPEND SLOTS ON IT. (a) secp256k1 has PRIME group order, hence no point of order 2 or 4, hence NO Montgomery form and no Edwards form over Fp — the classic Montgomery xz-ladder simply does not exist for this curve. (b) Brier-Joye x-only differential addition DOES work on any short Weierstrass curve, but its whole point is avoiding inversions, and in R1CS an inversion is ~1 allocation + 1 constraint (hint inv, enforce x*inv=1) — nearly free — so projective (X:Z) trades cheap inversions for extra non-native MULTIPLICATIONS, each ~730 rows (mulModSub2Cost 728/734). A 256-bit x-only ladder at ~10 field muls per bit is ~2560 mul-mods ~ 1.9M rows, versus 563079 for the current GLV+window circuit. The RIGHT reading of 'work on one coordinate' in this cost model is NOT a ladder but lambda-deferral: keep (x, lambda) through the loop and materialize y once (see the halo2 entry above).
GLV: decompose k = k1 + k2*lambda (mod n) into two ~128-bit halves; the endomorphism psi(x,y)=(beta*x mod p, y) costs ~6 constraints; then k*P = k1*P + k2*psi(P) halves the number of doublings.

GLV-3 / higher-dimensional decomposition (eprint 2025/1151, 2025/933): split k into THREE ~85-bit sub-scalars using the endomorphism twice (k = k0 + k1*lambda + k2*lambda^2 mod n); ~85 doublings instead of ~128, run as a joint 3-MSM sharing every doubling. Fewer doublings = fewer non-native Fp ops.

Find SHORTEST decomposition vectors via integer lattice reduction or a half-extended Euclidean algorithm in the endomorphism ring (eprint 2025/933); secp256k1's small CM discriminant (D=-3, j=0) admits extra reductions (reported 22-53% proving-time drop vs prior SOTA).
Run the decomposed halves/thirds as a width-w windowed joint-MSM (double-then-add) sharing doublings — reference figure ~2176 constraints for the 2-MSM core.
Per scalar bit the naive cost is ~4 (point selects) + ~4 (adds) + ~2 (double); wNAF / signed-digit windows cut the number of ADDITIONS via longer zero runs.

PRIME-REDUCE for a FIXED prime (circom-ecdsa): do limb mul/add WITHOUT carries into a wide form (k=4 x 64-bit registers for 256-bit; a product spans ~10 registers), then collapse 10 registers back to 4 in ONE reduction (~1000 constraints) by subtracting PRECOMPUTED multiples of p — compile-time constants because p is fixed. DEFERRAL BUDGET: keep 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < 254 (native field bits); that inequality tells you exactly how many unreduced products you may accumulate before a carry/reduce pass is actually required — defer right up to it, not further.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce, ~2x fewer reductions): accumulate a*b +/- c*d in WIDE UNREDUCED limbs and reduce ONCE at the end. Affine EC formulas are exactly this shape — lambda = (y2-y1)*inv(x2-x1), x3 = lambda^2 - x1 - x2, y3 = lambda*(x1-x3) - y1 — so reduce once PER OUTPUT COORDINATE, never per intermediate product.

COORDINATE-SYSTEM TRAP: in R1CS an inversion costs ~1 allocation + 1 constraint (hint inv as a witness, enforce x*inv = 1), so division is nearly FREE here — the opposite of the software cost model. Jacobian/projective/co-Z formulas (incl. Meloni co-Z ladders at ~11M+5S+23A per scalar bit) exist ONLY to avoid inversion, and pay for it with extra MULTIPLICATIONS — which are the expensive non-native op in-circuit. Prefer plain AFFINE add/double with hinted inverses; do NOT port inversion-free coordinate systems from the ECC literature.
Use INCOMPLETE / affine addition formulas (cheaper than complete-addition) where exceptional cases are ruled out by the decomposition, guarded by a soundness argument.

Precomputed-points-as-HINTS (eprint 2025/933): compute the scalar-mul result and per-step accumulator points OUTSIDE the circuit and pass them as witnesses; the circuit only CHECKS each group-law relation, which is cheaper than deriving points in-circuit. The prior R1CS baseline was ~9 constraints per scalar bit — beat that per bit.

AUDIT FOR OVER-ALLOCATION in the incomplete-add ladder (circom-ecdsa finding): only the first ~3 steps actually need the complete-addition guard, so accumulator/point arrays sized [bits] can be cut to [bits-3] and [3]. Allocations are HALF the cost metric here — sweep every witness array for entries that are never constrained or never read.

Non-native Fp: minimal-limb schoolbook mul + reduce with carry-save accumulation and top-bit-fold limb range checks; the flexible-limb EqViaCarries family (see reference/) may pack the equality check tighter.
secp256k1-fixed-base-scalar-mul: THE COMPLETE ADDITION IS ALREADY GONE — THE NEXT WIN IS FOLDING THE FINAL ADD INTO THE CHAIN (measured on the 82637 seed, verify against your copy). Live cost split (alloc+constr): 19 chain steps 68723 (83.2%), FinalAdd 6851 (8.3%), ChainStart 2902, ChainFinish 1467, 2 window selects 1368, 2 Canonicalize 1304, TopSelect 22, Recode 0. FinalAdd ALREADY replaces complete addition with exception special-casing: indicators for the three exceptional scalars (order n; 2^253-2; the odd doubling scalar), a Mux routing A to a safe point, ONE IncompleteAdd, and a Mux routing the constant answer back — and that exception machinery costs only 46 rows total (EitherZero 3/3, two IsZeroField 2/2, two AffPoint Mux 8/8). So exception handling is NOT the cost; the materialized affine add is: IncompleteAdd alone is 3384 alloc + 3421 constr = 6805, versus 2933 for a chain EXTENSION step (ChainExt 1462/1471), because the chain carries an (x, lambda) representation and materializes y ONCE in ChainFinish. LEVER: make the top window a 20th CHAIN step in (x, lambda) form instead of a separate materialized affine addition, applying the SAME cheap indicator+Mux exception guard in lambda space (mux over (x,lam) is as cheap as over (x,y); the special points are compile-time constants). That trades FinalAdd's 6805 for ~2933, roughly 3900 rows (~4.7% of the whole circuit). Keep ChainFinish as the single y-materialization. Do NOT reintroduce CompleteAdd: Step.lean/ScalarMul.lean still reference it but are DEAD code, unreachable from Main.

OFFSET THE CONSTANT TABLE SO NO WINDOW CAN HIT AN EXCEPTIONAL CASE (halo2 fixed-base gadget): define window w's table as M[w][k] = [(k+2)*(2^wbits)^w]G rather than [k*(2^wbits)^w]G. The +2 does two things: k=0 no longer selects the IDENTITY (so no add-with-infinity guard is needed anywhere), and it kills the collision that a +1 offset would leave (k0=7 with k1=0 would both select [8]G, forcing a DOUBLING, which incomplete addition cannot perform). With every selected point guaranteed non-identity and distinct from the accumulator, the ENTIRE ladder can use incomplete/affine addition with NO complete-add guards and no exception branches — pure constraint savings. Correct the accumulated offset inside the LAST window: M[W-1][k] = [k*(2^wbits)^(W-1) - sum_{j<W-1}(2^wbits)^{j+1}]G, itself a compile-time constant, so the correction is FREE.

Base G is FIXED: every window multiple j*(2^{w*i})*G is a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT — bake the whole comb table into the circuit as constants (zero constraints to build it), unlike the variable-base case.
Comb method: k = sum b_{i} 2^{i}; group bits into d combs of width w so each step is ONE table select + ONE add; fewer adds than plain windowed double-and-add.
Width-w NAF / signed-digit recoding of the scalar so table entries cover +/- multiples, halving table size and generating more zero (skip) positions.

Signed-digit tables cost almost nothing to apply: -P = (x, -y), so the sign bit drives ONE modular negation of y (an affine op), NOT a second multiplexer. So a width-w signed table needs only 2^{w-1} constant entries selected, plus a conditional y-negation — half the select cost of an unsigned width-w table for the same window count.
Constant-table point selection as a multiplexer over field constants: select cost is linear in window size but touches only additions/booleans, no non-native mul.

PRIME-REDUCE for a FIXED prime (circom-ecdsa): do limb mul/add WITHOUT carries into a wide form (k=4 x 64-bit registers for 256-bit; a product spans ~10 registers), then collapse 10 registers back to 4 in ONE reduction (~1000 constraints) by subtracting PRECOMPUTED multiples of p — compile-time constants because p is fixed. DEFERRAL BUDGET: keep 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < 254 (native field bits); that inequality tells you exactly how many unreduced products you may accumulate before a carry/reduce pass is actually required — defer right up to it, not further.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce, ~2x fewer reductions): accumulate a*b +/- c*d in WIDE UNREDUCED limbs and reduce ONCE at the end. Affine EC formulas are exactly this shape — lambda = (y2-y1)*inv(x2-x1), x3 = lambda^2 - x1 - x2, y3 = lambda*(x1-x3) - y1 — so reduce once PER OUTPUT COORDINATE, never per intermediate product.

COORDINATE-SYSTEM TRAP: in R1CS an inversion costs ~1 allocation + 1 constraint (hint inv as a witness, enforce x*inv = 1), so division is nearly FREE here — the opposite of the software cost model. Jacobian/projective/co-Z formulas (incl. Meloni co-Z ladders at ~11M+5S+23A per scalar bit) exist ONLY to avoid inversion, and pay for it with extra MULTIPLICATIONS — which are the expensive non-native op in-circuit. Prefer plain AFFINE add/double with hinted inverses; do NOT port inversion-free coordinate systems from the ECC literature.

Combine comb sub-scalars as a joint accumulation sharing point doublings/additions (multi-comb), analogous to the joint-MSM trick, so the fixed precompute is amortized across all windows in one add-chain.

Port secp256k1-scalar-mul's GroupedEqXV / MulModTarget non-native machinery (see reference/) if it lowers the per-add Fp mul-mod cost below the current Flex path; competitor csko pushed this challenge to 90041, a large structural gap — a comb-table + incomplete-add rewrite is likely needed, not incremental tweaks.

GLV IS STRICTLY BETTER ON A FIXED BASE — and is missing from this solution's playbook. Decompose k = k1 + k2*lambda (mod n) into two ~128-bit halves. Because the base is FIXED, lambda*G is itself a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT: unlike the variable-base case there is NO in-circuit endomorphism to evaluate (variable-base pays ~6 constraints for psi(x,y)=(beta*x, y); here it costs ZERO). You get TWO constant comb tables (multiples of G and of lambda*G), both free to build, and run them as a JOINT accumulation sharing every doubling — roughly halving the add/double chain. The only in-circuit cost is checking the decomposition: k1 + k2*lambda = k (mod n) plus range checks on k1,k2 — one non-native relation, not per-bit work.

Push the same idea further: with all tables being compile-time constants there is no table-size penalty for HIGHER-DIMENSIONAL decomposition (GLV-3 via lambda^2, or 4-dimensional GLV). Each extra dimension shortens the sub-scalars (256 -> ~128 -> ~85 -> ~64 bits) and shortens the shared doubling chain proportionally, at the cost only of more CONSTANT tables (free) and a slightly bigger decomposition check. Sweep the dimension and pick the minimum of (doublings + selects + decomposition check).

mLSB-set comb is the standard pairing of comb methods with GLV curves (see the fixed-base comb / GLV-GLS literature) — combine mLSB-set recoding with the two (or more) constant tables rather than treating comb and GLV as alternatives.
gf2-k12-compress-canonical: GF(2) CHANGES THE COST MODEL: every element IS a bit, so booleanity constraints vanish entirely — the ONLY cost is chi's multiplication. theta/rho/pi/iota are all F2-LINEAR (XOR = addition, rotation = index permutation, round constant = affine offset) and must cost ZERO.
Baseline 38400 = 12 rounds x 1600 bits x (1 alloc + 1 constraint) — exactly ONE multiplication per state bit. Beating it means beating the MULTIPLICATIVE COMPLEXITY of chi, not shaving overhead.

chi over GF(2): chi_i = a_i + a_{i+2} + a_{i+1}*a_{i+2} (since NOT b = 1+b is affine). Per 5-bit row the products are a1a2,a2a3,a3a4,a4a0,a0a1 — 5 products for 5 outputs, each seemingly used once. LOOK FOR: an algebraic identity computing all 5 row outputs with FEWER than 5 multiplications, products shared between adjacent rows/slices, or a change of basis making chi cheaper.
Only 12 rounds (KangarooTwelve), not 24 — half the rounds of keccak-f1600, so per-round savings are worth proportionally more of the total.

FINAL-ROUND TRIM: the last round's chi feeds only the output. Check whether any intermediate there can be left unmaterialized, or whether the output bits can BE the product witnesses rather than separate allocations — allocations are half the score.

An allocation is only needed for a value that a rank-1 product must reference. Any bit expressible as an affine combination of existing witnesses needs NO allocation — over GF(2) that covers all of theta/rho/pi/iota, so the allocation count should equal the MULTIPLICATION count exactly, never more.

MULTIPLICATIVE-COMPLEXITY FLOOR (SAT-solver literature, FSE 2016 'Optimizing S-Box Implementations ... Using SAT Solvers' and eprint 2023/1721 revisit): the Keccak 5-bit chi S-box has a PROVABLY MINIMAL nonlinear-gate count of 5 — implementations with 5 AND/NCT gates are known and SAT-proven optimal. So 5 muls per 5-bit row x 320 rows = 1600 multiplications per round is a HARD FLOOR for the constraint side; do NOT burn effort hunting a 4-multiplication chi row, it does not exist.

THEREFORE the remaining lever is the ALLOCATION side, not the constraint side. Constraints are pinned at 19200 (12 x 1600 products). The score is allocations+constraints = 38400, so any win must come from allocating FEWER than 19200 witnesses. chi_i = a_i + a_{i+2} + a_{i+1}*a_{i+2} is AFFINE in the product, so only the PRODUCT needs a witness — never allocate the chi output itself. Audit for: outputs materialized separately from their product witness, the final round's 1600 outputs (can they BE product witnesses?), and any witness the mechanical dead-variable pass would delete.

Cross-round product reuse is the only other opening: the linear layer (theta/rho/pi) between rounds mixes lanes, so a product from round r is generally NOT reusable in round r+1 — verify this rather than assume it, but expect no win there.
gf2-sha256-compress-canonical: GF(2): bits are free of booleanity; XOR/rotate/shift are FREE affine combinations. Cost concentrates in (a) AND gates in Ch/Maj and (b) the mod-2^32 ADDITION carry chains, which are NOT linear over GF(2) and usually dominate.
Minimum-AND forms: Ch(e,f,g) = g + e*(f+g) is ONE multiplication. Maj(a,b,c) = a*b + c*(a+b) is TWO; the symmetric ab+ac+bc form costs three — always use the factored version.

CORRECTION — CARRY-SAVE IS NOT A WIN OVER GF(2): a full-adder carry is maj(a,b,cin) = ab + cin(a+b) = ONE multiplication, so a 32-bit mod-2^32 addition costs 31 muls (carries c_1..c_31), and a 3:2 compressor row ALSO costs 31. Reducing k addends therefore costs (k-1)*31 either way — carry-save buys DEPTH, not AND-count. Its advantage in large-field R1CS comes from avoiding range checks, which do not exist here. Do NOT restructure the adder tree expecting a win; the lever is FEWER ADDITIONS and SHARED carry subexpressions, not a different tree shape.

A full-adder carry over GF(2) is maj(a,b,cin) = ab + cin(a+b) — ONE multiplication; the sum bit a+b+cin is free. So a 32-bit ripple costs ~32 muls, and a 3:2 compressor costs 32 muls while removing an entire addend.

Baseline 95904 vs record 44784 — a >2x gap, so the record is NOT using a naive per-addend ripple. Assume a carry-save tree plus minimum-AND Ch/Maj, and look for further sharing of carry subexpressions across the 64 rounds.

Reference point: Flock's pinned SHA-256 R1CS encoder is 30,632 allocations + 30,632 constraints = 61,264 interface-normalized — already beaten by the 44784 record, so treat 61k as a floor to clear, not a goal.

MC FLOOR ARITHMETIC (Boyar-Peralta full-adder/half-adder optimality): count the mandatory multiplications. Per round T1 = h+Sigma1(e)+Ch+K+W is 4 adds = 124, Ch = 32, T2 = Sigma0(a)+Maj is 1 add = 31, Maj = 64, a=T1+T2 = 31, e=d+T1 = 31 -> ~313 muls/round x 64 = ~20.0k; message schedule 3 adds x 31 x 48 = ~4.5k; final 8-word add = 248. Naive total ~24.7k muls -> score ~49.5k. The record is 44780, BELOW that — so the record IS sharing work across rounds. Find the sharing; the adder shape alone will not get you there.

Where the sharing must be: (a) Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1 are free affine rotations — never allocate them; (b) K_t is a CONSTANT so h+K_t is affine, folding one whole addend out of T1's chain; (c) adding a constant costs FEWER than 31 muls because carries into known-zero constant bits are determined — specialize the adder per round constant instead of using a generic 32-bit adder; (d) reuse carry bits between the T1 chain and the e=d+T1 / a=T1+T2 adds where operands coincide.

OPTIMAL COUNTERS BEAT FULL-ADDER CHAINS (Boyar-Peralta, 'The Exact Multiplicative Complexity of the Hamming Weight Function'): MC of the Hamming weight of n bits is EXACTLY n - H(n), where H(n) is the Hamming weight of n's binary representation. Multi-operand addition is column-wise Hamming-weight counting, so a k:log(k) COUNTER is the right primitive, not a chain of 3:2 full adders. Check: k=3 gives 3-H(3)=1 (a full adder, 1 AND — consistent); k=7 gives 7-H(7)=4 ANDs for a 7:3 counter, strictly better than chaining full adders over the same 7 bits. SHA-256 sums 5 addends in T1 plus incoming carries, so columns are 5-7 bits deep — build OPTIMAL COUNTERS per column and let carries propagate between columns, rather than adding operands two at a time. This is the standard AND-minimisation technique and is the most likely source of the large structural drops competitors are landing.
